BEITBRIDGE BORDER BALLS UP ROUND 2

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We take you to the Beitbridge Border and bring you a story of broken system that is being milked by the corrupt who exploit the desperate and the vulnerable.

Unique Selling Point:
** UNDERCOVER INVESTIGATION EXPOSING GROSS ABUSE OF POWER AT THE HANDS OF SANDF MEMBERS
** VISUALLY INTERESTING STORY WITH PRESENTER DRIVEN STORY TELLING
** TAKING A NEWS ANGLE STORY AND ELEVATING IT TO AN INVESTIGATIVE PIECE

Summary:
This is a story of broken system that is being milked by the corrupt who exploit the desperate and the vulnerable.

WE did the story last year about the 40km border fence that cost a whopping R37 million to erect. It was a very basic barb wire fence. At the time, there were already visible holes cut through the fence. Now the fence is gone. And it’s a free for all, who are forced to grease the palms of SANDF members to look the other way, while trucks line up for kilometers with backlogs at the Beitbridge Border Post.

While the system is crippled, the vultures circle. We’re talking undercover investigation and the shock of border control process that is on the brink of collapse.


Further information:
FAST FORWARD 15 MONTHS FROM OUR LAST PIECE …. there is very little left of the fence – just a few poles. But it’s basically open for large stretches of the 40km border line. The trucks that were lined up for kilometers and kilometers when the border was closed during the height of the lockdown – are still standing for kilometers and kilometers, now not because of COVID regulations, but because of an inefficient processing system and of course because of corrupt elements.

In recent months trucks could jump the queue for a fee, but transporters that are playing by the rules have had enough and have started blocking off the road in both directions. A round trip that should take 3 days max is taking up to a week if not more – breaking transport companies that are already struggling in a tough market. I am working on getting footage of a bribe – but with tensions between transporters mounting – the corruption element has taken a back seat at the moment. Drivers are getting confrontational with those that try to jump the line and fears of violence are mounting. In the last two weeks even the bribing has come to a halt with all lanes blocked off – there isn’t even room to jump the queue even if you wanted to pay.

Locals can’t even drive on the roads, they have to travel on dirt roads along the tar road to get from point to point.

While these trucks are backlogged - people and supplies are crossing the border illegally, day in and day out. More than ever it’s become a lucrative income stream for the SANDF. They have upped their game by demanding bribes every day from grocery smugglers who take food and supplies across from SA to Zim. THIS IS NOT NEW. But we have never shown the SANDF taking bribes.

It’s a humanitarian crisis that has escalated in recent months, while corrupt official abuse their power and profit from government ineffectiveness.

ELEMENTS / SCENES / VOICES
- VOX POPS WITH DRIVERS ON THE BORDER SITTING IN THE BACKLOG
- RIDE ALONG WITH ONE OF THE TRANSPORTER’S FOOD TRUCKS TO SHOW THE FRUSTRATION AND IMPACT ON TRANSPORTERS – COVID TESTS // DAYS LOST SPENT WAITING //
- ROAD FREIGHT ASSOCIATION – GAVIN KELLY – ** WE’LL ZOOM HIM FROM THE BORDER WITH TRUCK BACKLOG - HE IS A GREAT VOICE FOR THE INDUSTRY CAPTURES THE CHALLENGES AT BEITBRIDGE – HE SAYS SIMILAR SITUATION AT MOZAMBIQUE BORDERS – NOT SA ISSUE, INEFFECTIVE SYSTEMS ON THE OTHER SIDE – WILL COVER THE CUSTOMS // CLEARING AGENT SIDE
- LOCAL SECURITY COMPANY / VOICE FOR MUSINA RESIDENTS – IZAK NEL – CHALLENGES OF BACKLOGS, THE FENCE THAT DOESN’T EXISIT // CRIME ON THE RISE – WE’RE GOING TO TRY AND GO INTO THE SMUGGLING POINTS
- SMUGGLER - HIDDEN ID – WILL TELL ABOUT THE BRIBING
- UNDERCOVER BUYS
- JAKKIE CILLIERS – INSTITUTE FOR SECURITY STUDIES – ISSUE AROUND A MILITARY THAT EXPLOIT THE PEOPLE THEY ARE MEANT TO PROTECT (RATHER HAVE JAKKIE THAN THE CLEARING AGENT ASSOCIATION – OUR SCOOP IS THE SANDF)
- SANDF – CONFRONT

** I’M NOT GOING TO WORK ON THE BEITBRIDGE CUSTOMS INSIDER – WE HAVE 8 ELEMENTS HERE AND STILL NEED TO RECAP THE ISSUES WITH THE FENCE THAT WAS SHIT TO START WITH AND IS NOW GONE.

INVESTIGATIVE POTENTIAL
COMMISSIONED AT 12 as a starting point. I did mention yesterday that this feels like it has investigative potential – there has been the extra work with regards to working sources and my resources for getting the undercover elements and smuggler in the bag. But will raise this at the viewing again and then you can decide.




Extra Budget Items:
** TRAVEL TO MUSINA – I will use my car because the roads are tough there and a corolla won’t cope on the road next to the fence where we will be playing for most of the shoot.
** ACCOMMODATION – presenter, cameraman & producer
** EXTRA SHOOT DAY WITH PRESENTER (I will cover the 3rd day with cameraman)
** I HAVE COVERED THE INVESTIGATIVE ELEMENTS SO FAR - in terms of my hidden camera being used and my contacts helping me get the undercover in the bag

Script:


STRUCTURE – 14 min

VO: Musina, the northernmost town in South Africa is not immune to controversy.

June 2020. Beitbridge Border. A 40 kilometer razor wire fence was erected during the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic, to secure a section of the South Africa - Zimbabwe border line. The projected price tag? A whopping R37 million.

UPSOUND OLD CARTE BLANCHE JUNE 2020
MAC LINK: Some would argue it's a steep price for something that's clearly not serving its purpose.

VO: Fast Forward to October 2021 and the media cast the spotlight on inefficiencies at Beitbridge Border Post. Infrastructure upgrades and an administration fault on the Zimbabwean side, resulted in a 15 kilometre gridlock that saw drivers stranded for two and a half weeks.

Gavin Kelly from the Road Freight Association says the backlog had a crippling impact on the transport industry.

GAVIN: Depending on the size of the truck, every day that you stand can cost you about 3500 to 7000 rand// You haven't been able to generate that revenue.

VO: Eventually a Zim task team was called in and trucks flew through the border – clearing the backlog in just a day. Everything seemingly returned to normal and the media moved on.

Our months-long investigation took us to the west and east of the border post. This is a story about corrupt role players, who like vultures circle and exploit a broken border security system.

LINK: While the roads to BeitBridge may have been cleared for the time being, the dust has not settled on the illegal cross-border trade that appears to keep the wheels turning at this border.

VO: A year and half after our first story, on the controversial fence that cost just under a million rand per kilometre to put up – this….. is what is left of it.

LINK: Look at this. They've stolen the poles and they've cut up the fence into sections, the thieves roll the fence and they literally stealing the fence. Bit by bit.

VO: In 2020 already, questions were raised over whether the project was necessary, whether it was priced correctly and whether the contract was awarded fairly. Earlier this year, a damning report by the Special Investigations Unit confirmed, there were irregularities.

JAKKIE: It's a diversion of responsibility and just ducking and diving, which I think is really problematic.

VO: Border Security Expert, Jakkie Cilliers believes the South African government’s current border control measures are flawed.

JAKKIE: // It was a political reaction against a rising tide of xenophobia in South Africa that we have to keep foreigners out What is much more problematic here is the conceptualization of this misuse of public funding for absolutely a political purpose that has no practical chance of ever succeeding.

VO: The border is crossed illegally every single day without fail.

But not everyone who crosses is moving contraband, with prices skyrocketing in Zimbabwe, and supplies running low – smuggling food and building material has become an essential service on this borderline.

These people are carriers – they physically run goods across the border, for a fee.

CLAIRE: Sanbonani….//I want to know, brother, if I have stuff to cross over – how much is it?
CARRIER: R100 , R100
CLAIRE: How much for what? for how much?
CARRIER: It depends how heavy it is.
CLAIRE: // what’s the maximum price
CARRIER: Allright, the maximum is R250, but there are different prices.
CLAIRE: You take anything? clothes, food...everything?
CARRIER: Food and clothes, everything we carrier it.

VO: These goods don’t go through the border post legitimately; it goes around it, through the R37 million fence.

LINK: We've just come across people smuggling groceries across from South Africa to Zimbabwe across this very porous border. They have seen us yet it continues unabated.

VO: It’s clear, that while the formal border post remains closed off to non-essential human traffic, the borderline was in no way closed off.

JAKKIE: people in Zimbabwe and in the rest of Africa are struggling. They come to South Africa to shop, to survive, to seek work.

VO: The South African National Defence Force, or SANDF is tasked with monitoring the borderline Brigadier General Mafi Mgobozi concedes the fence is not up to scratch.

BRIG GEN: the state of the fence which was put, we have seen that that is not in a good condition to be a BORDER FENCE
CLAIRE: Some of the big holes and the gaps in the fence are hundreds of metres away from the SANDF
BRIG GEN: It is not the responsibility of the SAN defence force to close all those holes. our troops which are deployed, they are trying by all means to do their job to ensure that they are no people coming in into South Africa. And then there are not people who are going out illegally.

VO: But locals will tell you, that’s not what’s happening on the ground. For fear of retribution, this frustrated Musina resident spoke to us on condition of anonymity.

RESIDENT: They're not monitoring that a road // they have no measures in place to effectively force control over the border.

VO: This man is a smuggler - he crosses between Zim and South Africa – illegally – every day – without being questioned by authorities. He says demand is high, business is booming and passport checks are never an issue.

CLAIRE: do you know it’s illegal
SMUGGLER: Yah, we know, but I want money
CLAIRE: how much earning
SMUGGLER: Sometimes when it’s not busy, maybe it’s like R450 or R400, but sometimes when it’s busy I can make R1050 to R1500
CLAIRE: in one day?
SMUGGLER: That R1050 is maybe after three hours – if it’s busy, obviously I can make more.

RESIDENT: It's a free for all. It's a daily occurrence, even an hourly occurrence. Everyone knows what’s happening.

VO: Over the last year – cross border smuggling has spiked dramatically on the military’s watch. Brigadier General Mgobozi feels the odds are stacked against them.

BRIG GEN: along the border, I suppose of 22, companies only have 15 companies. Because we don't have enough numbers, people, they use those GAPS. The budget cut, I think you will understand that Our budget AS SANDF every year is going down, down, down

VO: But our investigation revealed it goes beyond a lack of resources and manpower. This footage was recorded by an undercover operative at one of the many smuggling points on the border line. Our investigation confirmed blatant military inaction.

Watch how goods are moved while a SANDF member just looks on – boxes, appliances – it’s a constant flurry of illicit activity – all under the watchful eye of an armed soldier.

We showed our footage to Brigadier General Mgobozi.

CLAIRE: Smugglers in broad daylight and the SANDF member iS THERE
BRIG GEN: we have those people, will call the rotten apples within the SANDF. they go and allow people to go up and down like that, and then they are standing in front of and looking //it means is assisting them, by standing there he is assisting them

VO: Cilliers is adamant border control, should not be optional, it is a basic function of statehood, irrespective of the humanitarian crisis in neighbouring countries.

JAKKIE: having that empathy doesn't absolve the primary responsibility of government to look after its own citizens first. // People can't just walk across the border. No country in the world allows that, and South Africa cannot, either.

VO: In the time we did the interview, 12 fully loaded vehicles passed behind us on the border road.

LINK: Just to be clear, the road behind me is not a public road, access to it is limited to military or to farmers living adjacent to the border line. But these aren't farmers or military. They smugglers who are moving across the border. Day in, day out illegally.

CLAIRE: In a matter of 20 minutes, 12 cars loaded heavily with goods that we could see groceries, building materials // passed while we were standing there
BRIG GEN: THAT Was A NEGLECTION OF DUTIES

VO: Interestingly, the steady flow of vehicles stopped as we were packing up gear. Shortly afterwards, three soldiers approached us on foot and questioned our crew.

SOLDIER: I heard that you are filming from the cars are passing here?
PRODUCER: The smuggling cars, Sir?
SOLDIER: yes
PRODUCER: That are smuggling?
SOLDIER: yes. We don’t know if they are smuggling or not – some of them have got permits to pass here.
PRODUCER: we’re allowed to film, but we’re not trespassing
SOLDIER: are you allowed to do that?
PRODCUER: we have permission to be on this farm.

VO: As the soldiers were actually the ones trespassing on private land, they took our details and left.

We went to the gate that we had breezed through the previous day, to check what the sudden hold up was with fully loaded cars lining up. The drivers were not that chatty.

CLAIRE: Guys why you like this? I just want to know why you are waiting….
LINK: They were relaxed and as soon as we came with the cameras they decided not to speak to us// People are hiding their identities, hiding their faces. They don't want to speak to media.

VO: The military were not happy with our presence here either….

UPSOUND
SOLDIER – this place were the soldiers are operating – you must have a permission

CLAIRE: What we understand as media – we can shoot in public places and in public property – where we are right now and where these people are sitting….

VO: They insisted that we needed special permission. As we walked off the cars started turning around.

LINK: And just like that everyone cleared out.

VO: We shared our experience with Brigadier General Mgobozi.

CLAIRE: they had been chasing us all day. They had been chasing us. They stopped us when they weren't supposed to stop us on private land, on public roads. They knew we were filming. // Suddenly, // protocol was being observed. And I do believe that it was because we were there
BRIG GEN: It’s not because you were there, they were doing their job as they know what they must do.
CLAIRE: And then the day before, what were they doing?
BRIG GEN: Let me say that that those guys, they know what they must do. They just neglected their duty.
CLAIRE: For months, they just neglected the duty for months, for months
BRIG GEN: Not say for months you were there for two days.

VO: Our investigation actually kicked off two months before filming.

And we have proof that it’s not simply a neglect of duty - it’s more sinister. The illicit transportation of goods is a lucrative income stream - not just for the smugglers.…

Watch this video clip. The soldier is negotiating // with a smuggler. Not happy with the discussion, he stops the carriers from moving the goods.

SMUGGLER: When we move things, we negotiate with the soldiers and then we give them something.
CLAIRE: something like what? Malini? How much do they ask for/
SMUGGLER: Now, one car load, can be either R100 or R50.

VO: After a while, the smuggler returns. Watch how the soldier takes his bribe. And just like, the smuggling continues with the blessing of the SANDF.

CLAIRE: is that shocking for you?
BRIG GEN: I'm shocked to see what this member is doing, what he's doing is I will call him is a criminal.

VO: But the Brigadier General was quick to lay blame with the smugglers.

BRIG GEN: The person who's going to go and want to cross with certain stuff along the border. He knows that, first of all, he's doing the illegal thing
CLAIRE: CORRECT
BRIG GEN: That is why you would want to bribe the soldier because you don't want to be ARRESTED.…..
CLAIRE: the soldiers also bribe- able - Do you understand? So, it takes two for corruption to happen the corrupt and the corruptee? it's a deal.
BRIG GEN: Not all our soldiers are like that. //There are those who are dedicated. And then there are those some, //I would say sometimes this syndicate because you cannot work alone when you are doing this.

VO: Even if all of the soldiers in Musina aren’t on the take, they are not exposing the culprits either - making them complicit.

RESIDENT: they are basically just a corrupt bunch, ///They are not here to protect us. We as a community are afraid // it's escalating and escalating // They disregard the entire situation, the military. // It's open as daylight and nothing is being done.

VO: Brigadier General Mgobozi promised that these allegations will not be taken lightly and action would be imminent.

BRIG GEN: They are doing their thing against the CODE, against the mission, which they have been giving, that you must go and protect the borders of South Africa. we won't allow CERTAIN individualS // to tarnish the image of the staff of National Defence Force.

VO: Cilliers believes it’s a sign of the times, there has been a general decline in discipline in the country’s law enforcement agencies.

JAKKIE: Corruption has become a rife in South Africa because we we don't hold people to account. // There must be consequences. Nobody has a problem with a country, humanely and decently enforcing its own sovereignty, because our primary responsibility is to South Africans.



 
PROMOS

PROMO 1 – 11 seconds
VO: We go inside smuggling rings on the South African Zimbabwe border and expose some national defence force soldiers that work with smugglers and shamelessly take bribes.


PROMO 2 – 21 seconds
VO: A two-month long investigation on the Zimbabwe – South Africa borderline uncovers how soldiers are lining their pocket with bribes from smugglers who cross illegally every single day.

RESIDENT: they are basically just a corrupt bunch, ///They are not here to protect us.

VO: We bring you this exclusive undercover investigation.

PROMO 3 – 21 seconds
VO: We go undercover on the border separating Zimbabwe and South Africa in Limpopo, where illegal crossings and corruption is the order of the day.

SMUGGLER: When we move things, we negotiate with the soldiers and then we give them something.

VO: We bring you “never before seen footage” of some SANDF soldiers taking bribes.

JAKKIE: // It was a political reaction against a rising tide of xenophobia in South Africa that we have to keep foreigners out What is much more problematic here is the conceptualization of this misuse of public funding for absolutely a political purpose that has no practical chance of ever succeeding. VO: The border is crossed illegally every single day without fail. But not everyone who crosses is moving contraband, with prices skyrocketing in Zimbabwe, and supplies running low – smuggling food and building material has become an essential service on this borderline. These people are carriers – they physically run goods across the border, for a fee. CLAIRE: Sanbonani….//I want to know, brother, if I have stuff to cross over – how much is it? CARRIER: R100 , R100 CLAIRE: How much for what? for how much? CARRIER: It depends how heavy it is. CLAIRE: // what’s the maximum price CARRIER: Allright, the maximum is R250, but there are different prices. CLAIRE: You take anything? clothes, food...everything? CARRIER: Food and clothes, everything we carrier it. VO: These goods don’t go through the border post legitimately; it goes around it, through the R37 million fence. LINK: We've just come across people smuggling groceries across from South Africa to Zimbabwe across this very porous border. They have seen us yet it continues unabated. VO: It’s clear, that while the formal border post remains closed off to non-essential human traffic, the borderline was in no way closed off. JAKKIE: people in Zimbabwe and in the rest of Africa are struggling. They come to South Africa to shop, to survive, to seek work. VO: The South African National Defence Force, or SANDF is tasked with monitoring the borderline Brigadier General Mafi Mgobozi concedes the fence is not up to scratch. BRIG GEN: the state of the fence which was put, we have seen that that is not in a good condition to be a BORDER FENCE CLAIRE: Some of the big holes and the gaps in the fence are hundreds of metres away from the SANDF BRIG GEN: It is not the responsibility of the SAN defence force to close all those holes. our troops which are deployed, they are trying by all means to do their job to ensure that they are no people coming in into South Africa. And then there are not people who are going out illegally. VO: But locals will tell you, that’s not what’s happening on the ground. For fear of retribution, this frustrated Musina resident spoke to us on condition of anonymity. RESIDENT: They're not monitoring that a road // they have no measures in place to effectively force control over the border. VO: This man is a smuggler - he crosses between Zim and South Africa – illegally – every day – without being questioned by authorities. He says demand is high, business is booming and passport checks are never an issue. CLAIRE: do you know it’s illegal SMUGGLER: Yah, we know, but I want money CLAIRE: how much earning SMUGGLER: Sometimes when it’s not busy, maybe it’s like R450 or R400, but sometimes when it’s busy I can make R1050 to R1500 CLAIRE: in one day? SMUGGLER: That R1050 is maybe after three hours – if it’s busy, obviously I can make more. RESIDENT: It's a free for all. It's a daily occurrence, even an hourly occurrence. Everyone knows what’s happening. VO: Over the last year – cross border smuggling has spiked dramatically on the military’s watch. Brigadier General Mgobozi feels the odds are stacked against them. BRIG GEN: along the border, I suppose of 22, companies only have 15 companies. Because we don't have enough numbers, people, they use those GAPS. The budget cut, I think you will understand that Our budget AS SANDF every year is going down, down, down VO: But our investigation revealed it goes beyond a lack of resources and manpower. This footage was recorded by an undercover operative at one of the many smuggling points on the border line. Our investigation confirmed blatant military inaction. Watch how goods are moved while a SANDF member just looks on – boxes, appliances – it’s a constant flurry of illicit activity – all under the watchful eye of an armed soldier. We showed our footage to Brigadier General Mgobozi. CLAIRE: Smugglers in broad daylight and the SANDF member iS THERE BRIG GEN: we have those people, will call the rotten apples within the SANDF. they go and allow people to go up and down like that, and then they are standing in front of and looking //it means is assisting them, by standing there he is assisting them VO: Cilliers is adamant border control, should not be optional, it is a basic function of statehood, irrespective of the humanitarian crisis in neighbouring countries. JAKKIE: having that empathy doesn't absolve the primary responsibility of government to look after its own citizens first. // People can't just walk across the border. No country in the world allows that, and South Africa cannot, either. VO: In the time we did the interview, 12 fully loaded vehicles passed behind us on the border road. LINK: Just to be clear, the road behind me is not a public road, access to it is limited to military or to farmers living adjacent to the border line. But these aren't farmers or military. They smugglers who are moving across the border. Day in, day out illegally. CLAIRE: In a matter of 20 minutes, 12 cars loaded heavily with goods that we could see groceries, building materials // passed while we were standing there BRIG GEN: THAT Was A NEGLECTION OF DUTIES VO: Interestingly, the steady flow of vehicles stopped as we were packing up gear. Shortly afterwards, three soldiers approached us on foot and questioned our crew. SOLDIER: I heard that you are filming from the cars are passing here? PRODUCER: The smuggling cars, Sir? SOLDIER: yes PRODUCER: That are smuggling? SOLDIER: yes. We don’t know if they are smuggling or not – some of them have got permits to pass here. PRODUCER: we’re allowed to film, but we’re not trespassing SOLDIER: are you allowed to do that? PRODCUER: we have permission to be on this farm. VO: As the soldiers were actually the ones trespassing on private land, they took our details and left. We went to the gate that we had breezed through the previous day, to check what the sudden hold up was with fully loaded cars lining up. The drivers were not that chatty. CLAIRE: Guys why you like this? I just want to know why you are waiting…. LINK: They were relaxed and as soon as we came with the cameras they decided not to speak to us// People are hiding their identities, hiding their faces. They don't want to speak to media. VO: The military were not happy with our presence here either…. UPSOUND SOLDIER – this place were the soldiers are operating – you must have a permission CLAIRE: What we understand as media – we can shoot in public places and in public property – where we are right now and where these people are sitting…. VO: They insisted that we needed special permission. As we walked off the cars started turning around. LINK: And just like that everyone cleared out. VO: We shared our experience with Brigadier General Mgobozi. CLAIRE: they had been chasing us all day. They had been chasing us. They stopped us when they weren't supposed to stop us on private land, on public roads. They knew we were filming. // Suddenly, // protocol was being observed. And I do believe that it was because we were there BRIG GEN: It’s not because you were there, they were doing their job as they know what they must do. CLAIRE: And then the day before, what were they doing? BRIG GEN: Let me say that that those guys, they know what they must do. They just neglected their duty. CLAIRE: For months, they just neglected the duty for months, for months BRIG GEN: Not say for months you were there for two days. VO: Our investigation actually kicked off two months before filming. And we have proof that it’s not simply a neglect of duty - it’s more sinister. The illicit transportation of goods is a lucrative income stream - not just for the smugglers.… Watch this video clip. The soldier is negotiating // with a smuggler. Not happy with the discussion, he stops the carriers from moving the goods. SMUGGLER: When we move things, we negotiate with the soldiers and then we give them something. CLAIRE: something like what? Malini? How much do they ask for/ SMUGGLER: Now, one car load, can be either R100 or R50. VO: After a while, the smuggler returns. Watch how the soldier takes his bribe. And just like, the smuggling continues with the blessing of the SANDF. CLAIRE: is that shocking for you? BRIG GEN: I'm shocked to see what this member is doing, what he's doing is I will call him is a criminal. VO: But the Brigadier General was quick to lay blame with the smugglers. BRIG GEN: The person who's going to go and want to cross with certain stuff along the border. He knows that, first of all, he's doing the illegal thing CLAIRE: CORRECT BRIG GEN: That is why you would want to bribe the soldier because you don't want to be ARRESTED.….. CLAIRE: the soldiers also bribe- able - Do you understand? So, it takes two for corruption to happen the corrupt and the corruptee? it's a deal. BRIG GEN: Not all our soldiers are like that. //There are those who are dedicated. And then there are those some, //I would say sometimes this syndicate because you cannot work alone when you are doing this. VO: Even if all of the soldiers in Musina aren’t on the take, they are not exposing the culprits either - making them complicit. RESIDENT: they are basically just a corrupt bunch, ///They are not here to protect us. We as a community are afraid // it's escalating and escalating // They disregard the entire situation, the military. // It's open as daylight and nothing is being done. VO: Brigadier General Mgobozi promised that these allegations will not be taken lightly and action would be imminent. BRIG GEN: They are doing their thing against the CODE, against the mission, which they have been giving, that you must go and protect the borders of South Africa. we won't allow CERTAIN individualS // to tarnish the image of the staff of National Defence Force. VO: Cilliers believes it’s a sign of the times, there has been a general decline in discipline in the country’s law enforcement agencies. JAKKIE: Corruption has become a rife in South Africa because we we don't hold people to account. // There must be consequences. Nobody has a problem with a country, humanely and decently enforcing its own sovereignty, because our primary responsibility is to South Africans. PROMOS PROMO 1 – 11 seconds VO: We go inside smuggling rings on the South African Zimbabwe border and expose some national defence force soldiers that work with smugglers and shamelessly take bribes. PROMO 2 – 21 seconds VO: A two-month long investigation on the Zimbabwe – South Africa borderline uncovers how soldiers are lining their pocket with bribes from smugglers who cross illegally every single day. RESIDENT: they are basically just a corrupt bunch, ///They are not here to protect us. VO: We bring you this exclusive undercover investigation. PROMO 3 – 21 seconds VO: We go undercover on the border separating Zimbabwe and South Africa in Limpopo, where illegal crossings and corruption is the order of the day. SMUGGLER: When we move things, we negotiate with the soldiers and then we give them something. VO: We bring you “never before seen footage” of some SANDF soldiers taking bribes.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We take you to the Beitbridge Border and bring you a story of broken system that is being milked by the corrupt who exploit the desperate and the vulnerable.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: ** UNDERCOVER INVESTIGATION EXPOSING GROSS ABUSE OF POWER AT THE HANDS OF SANDF MEMBERS ** VISUALLY INTERESTING STORY WITH PRESENTER DRIVEN STORY TELLING ** TAKING A NEWS ANGLE STORY AND ELEVATING IT TO AN INVESTIGATIVE PIECE
metadata.Summary: This is a story of broken system that is being milked by the corrupt who exploit the desperate and the vulnerable. WE did the story last year about the 40km border fence that cost a whopping R37 million to erect. It was a very basic barb wire fence. At the time, there were already visible holes cut through the fence. Now the fence is gone. And it’s a free for all, who are forced to grease the palms of SANDF members to look the other way, while trucks line up for kilometers with backlogs at the Beitbridge Border Post. While the system is crippled, the vultures circle. We’re talking undercover investigation and the shock of border control process that is on the brink of collapse.
metadata.Further information: FAST FORWARD 15 MONTHS FROM OUR LAST PIECE …. there is very little left of the fence – just a few poles. But it’s basically open for large stretches of the 40km border line. The trucks that were lined up for kilometers and kilometers when the border was closed during the height of the lockdown – are still standing for kilometers and kilometers, now not because of COVID regulations, but because of an inefficient processing system and of course because of corrupt elements. In recent months trucks could jump the queue for a fee, but transporters that are playing by the rules have had enough and have started blocking off the road in both directions. A round trip that should take 3 days max is taking up to a week if not more – breaking transport companies that are already struggling in a tough market. I am working on getting footage of a bribe – but with tensions between transporters mounting – the corruption element has taken a back seat at the moment. Drivers are getting confrontational with those that try to jump the line and fears of violence are mounting. In the last two weeks even the bribing has come to a halt with all lanes blocked off – there isn’t even room to jump the queue even if you wanted to pay. Locals can’t even drive on the roads, they have to travel on dirt roads along the tar road to get from point to point. While these trucks are backlogged - people and supplies are crossing the border illegally, day in and day out. More than ever it’s become a lucrative income stream for the SANDF. They have upped their game by demanding bribes every day from grocery smugglers who take food and supplies across from SA to Zim. THIS IS NOT NEW. But we have never shown the SANDF taking bribes. It’s a humanitarian crisis that has escalated in recent months, while corrupt official abuse their power and profit from government ineffectiveness. ELEMENTS / SCENES / VOICES - VOX POPS WITH DRIVERS ON THE BORDER SITTING IN THE BACKLOG - RIDE ALONG WITH ONE OF THE TRANSPORTER’S FOOD TRUCKS TO SHOW THE FRUSTRATION AND IMPACT ON TRANSPORTERS – COVID TESTS // DAYS LOST SPENT WAITING // - ROAD FREIGHT ASSOCIATION – GAVIN KELLY – ** WE’LL ZOOM HIM FROM THE BORDER WITH TRUCK BACKLOG - HE IS A GREAT VOICE FOR THE INDUSTRY CAPTURES THE CHALLENGES AT BEITBRIDGE – HE SAYS SIMILAR SITUATION AT MOZAMBIQUE BORDERS – NOT SA ISSUE, INEFFECTIVE SYSTEMS ON THE OTHER SIDE – WILL COVER THE CUSTOMS // CLEARING AGENT SIDE - LOCAL SECURITY COMPANY / VOICE FOR MUSINA RESIDENTS – IZAK NEL – CHALLENGES OF BACKLOGS, THE FENCE THAT DOESN’T EXISIT // CRIME ON THE RISE – WE’RE GOING TO TRY AND GO INTO THE SMUGGLING POINTS - SMUGGLER - HIDDEN ID – WILL TELL ABOUT THE BRIBING - UNDERCOVER BUYS - JAKKIE CILLIERS – INSTITUTE FOR SECURITY STUDIES – ISSUE AROUND A MILITARY THAT EXPLOIT THE PEOPLE THEY ARE MEANT TO PROTECT (RATHER HAVE JAKKIE THAN THE CLEARING AGENT ASSOCIATION – OUR SCOOP IS THE SANDF) - SANDF – CONFRONT ** I’M NOT GOING TO WORK ON THE BEITBRIDGE CUSTOMS INSIDER – WE HAVE 8 ELEMENTS HERE AND STILL NEED TO RECAP THE ISSUES WITH THE FENCE THAT WAS SHIT TO START WITH AND IS NOW GONE. INVESTIGATIVE POTENTIAL COMMISSIONED AT 12 as a starting point. I did mention yesterday that this feels like it has investigative potential – there has been the extra work with regards to working sources and my resources for getting the undercover elements and smuggler in the bag. But will raise this at the viewing again and then you can decide.
